change: The complete flat-list DOM/map proof uses one traversal-local expected-path cursor instead of allocating a new array for every node. The cursor is private and synchronous, never stored or returned. Every comparison retains astPathKey depth/index validation, exact reverse-path equality, DOM identity, shape, attributes, text, wrappers and placeholder checks. No validation cache, skipped subtree, public API, Rust, wire, selection-write or history changes.
verification: Strict browser source/test types and all 1870 browser unit tests pass.

New regression retains every mapped path across an ordered-list heading, empty item, root paragraph and trailing bullet list. Three full validations preserve distinct reverse-path identities, frozen state, exact indexes and forward mappings.
Private packed Node/types/Chromium base consumer and all three flat-list browser consumers pass. Shipping trees remained unchanged.

All 165 browser matrix cases and 54 list-demo cases pass across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with zero retries, failures, skips or suite errors. These ran concurrently on distinct ports only after performance measurements completed.
After all tests, the four shipping tree hashes still match and pmset reports no remaining caffeinate assertions; PreventSystemSleep and PreventUserIdleSystemSleep are both zero.

performance.method: Sequential baseline/candidate/baseline/candidate across three engines, then a reversed candidate/baseline WebKit-only pair. No concurrent Breditor builds/tests during measurements. Each run has three independent owners at each of 10, 100 and 500 items, exact selection/document/edit/undo/checkpoint/reload/redo assertions. All 126 correctness cases passed. Production minified fixture, bounded caffeinate -is assertions, one machine, uncontrolled external load; not p95 or a general latency guarantee.
performance.interpretation: Retain the small allocation reduction: WebKit large-list edit medians improve in both original pairs and the reversed-order pair. Chromium varies in both directions and Firefox is essentially unchanged. Other operations show noise and some overlapping/slightly worse ranges (including WebKit restore); this is not a blanket speedup or completion of the responsiveness gate. The intermittent WebKit selection/transport observation remains unresolved.

remaining: Intermittent WebKit faults are not claimed fixed by finite passing runs.
Physical-keyboard IME and audible VoiceOver qualification remain pending; prior temporary settings were restored.
Large-list Firefox responsiveness, approved optional delivery/size budgets and complete release qualification remain open.
